main.claim: Upload a voice note, or any audio file up to 15 MB, and get the words back in about 1 to 3 seconds. The text is word for word, in the language spoken, with punctuation and paragraph breaks. Free, with no account.

sections.heading: How to turn a voice note into text
sections.body:
This works for a WhatsApp voice note or any other audio file. You do not install anything and you do not sign in.

1. Open [Voice Note to Text](https://voice-note-to-text.lazur.app/).
2. Choose your voice note file. Audio files work, including .opus, .ogg and .m4a.
3. Wait about 1 to 3 seconds for the text to appear.
4. Copy the result with one click, then paste it into your message, note or document.

The tool takes files up to 15 MB. A file over that size is too big to upload, so use a shorter recording.

sections.heading: What you get back
sections.body:
The result is a word-for-word transcript in the language the person speaks. The tool adds punctuation and paragraph breaks, so a long voice note reads like text you wrote yourself.

If the file has no speech in it, the tool replies: No speech found. Play the file first to check that someone is talking, then try again with a recording that has a voice in it.

sections.heading: Free use and limits
sections.body:
You get 3 free runs a day. Leave an email and you get 3 more. You do not need an account, and you do not need an app.

The tool is most useful for a voice note you cannot listen to right now, such as a message during a meeting, or a recording you need as text for a reply or a note. A voice note usually comes back in about 1 to 3 seconds.

sections.heading: Where your voice note goes
sections.body:
This tool sends your file to Lazur's servers. There, Google Gemini transcribes it and returns the text to you. Before you upload a private recording, decide whether you are comfortable with that.

WhatsApp also has a transcript feature for voice messages you receive. WhatsApp says its transcripts are generated on your device. If you want the text to stay on your phone, use that feature when it is available to you. The steps are on the [WhatsApp voice to text not working](https://voice-note-to-text.lazur.app/not-working) page.

pages.description: WhatsApp voice to text not working? Turn on transcripts, match the language, and check your keyboard. If it still fails, transcribe the note free here.
pages.h1: WhatsApp voice to text not working
pages.claim: Turn on WhatsApp's voice message transcripts and match the language to the voice note. If a note still fails, save the file and transcribe it here free, with no account.

sections.heading: Turn on WhatsApp's transcripts
sections.body:
WhatsApp's voice message transcripts are off by default, so the first check is the setting.

1. Open WhatsApp and go to Settings.
2. Tap Chats.
3. Turn on Voice Message Transcripts.
4. Tap Choose language, then select the language most of your voice messages are in.

Transcripts only match the language you choose. If you get voice messages in two languages, a note in the other one can fail. Turning transcripts off resets the language, so set it again after you turn them back on.

sections.heading: Why a transcript says unavailable
sections.body:
WhatsApp's help page lists three causes for a transcript that cannot be read. The language you set does not match the voice message. Background noise makes some words hard to understand. The language of the voice message is not supported.

You cannot change the sound of a message someone sent you, so the fix is on your side. Set the right language. If the note is in a language WhatsApp does not support yet, use the free tool on a saved copy of the file instead.

sections.heading: Update WhatsApp
sections.body: WhatsApp says the feature may not be available to you yet, and that it only works on some devices. If the transcript settings are missing from your app, update WhatsApp to the latest version from your app store. Then open Settings, tap Chats, and check again.

sections.heading: If you mean the keyboard microphone
sections.body:
Some people mean the microphone on the keyboard, the one they tap to type a reply. That is a separate feature from transcripts, and it is set in your phone's keyboard settings.

On iPhone, the Dictate key is in the bottom-right corner of the keyboard. If you do not see it, open Settings, tap General, tap Keyboard, and turn on Enable Dictation. Apple's steps are on [Dictate text on iPhone](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/dictate-text-iph2c0651d2/ios).

On Android with Gboard, open any app where you can type, tap a text field, then tap the microphone at the top of the keyboard. Google says talk-to-text does not work with all languages. See [Type with your voice](https://support.google.com/gboard/answer/2781851?hl=en).

sections.heading: Transcribe the note here when WhatsApp cannot
sections.body:
When WhatsApp will not transcribe a note, save the voice note as a file and upload it to the free tool. The save option differs by phone and WhatsApp version, so look for a share or save option on the message.

1. Save the voice note as an audio file on your phone or computer.
2. Open [Voice Note to Text](https://voice-note-to-text.lazur.app/).
3. Choose the file. The tool takes audio up to 15 MB, including .opus, .ogg and .m4a.
4. Read the text, then copy it with one click.

You get 3 free runs a day, and 3 more if you leave an email. No account is needed.

sections.heading: What happens to the file
sections.body: The tool sends the file to Lazur's servers, where Google Gemini transcribes it. WhatsApp's own transcripts are generated on your device, according to WhatsApp. Pick the one that fits a private message before you upload it.

faq.q: Why isn't WhatsApp transcribing my voice messages?
faq.a: The most common reason is a setting. Open WhatsApp Settings, tap Chats, and make sure Voice Message Transcripts is on, with the language most of your voice messages use. If a note still shows unavailable, the language may not match, background noise may be too strong, or the language may not be supported yet.

faq.q: Why is my voice to text not working?
faq.a: If you mean WhatsApp transcripts, check the Chats setting and the language first. If you mean the keyboard microphone, turn on Dictation on iPhone under Settings, General, Keyboard, or tap the microphone at the top of the Gboard keyboard on Android. Those are separate from WhatsApp's transcripts.

faq.q: Why does my WhatsApp voice message say transcript unavailable?
faq.a: WhatsApp lists three causes: the language you set does not match the voice message, background noise makes some words hard to understand, or the language is not supported. Change the language setting, or save the note and transcribe it with the free tool.

pages.description: Does WhatsApp have voice to text? Yes, on some devices and languages. See the steps to turn it on, plus a free backup for notes it cannot read.
pages.h1: Does WhatsApp have voice to text?
pages.claim: Yes, on some devices and in some languages. WhatsApp can turn a received voice message into text when transcripts are on. If a note cannot be read that way, transcribe the saved file here free, with no account.

sections.heading: What WhatsApp's feature does
sections.body:
WhatsApp has voice message transcripts. They turn a voice message you receive into text, so you can read it when you cannot listen. WhatsApp says transcripts are generated on your device, so no one else, not even WhatsApp, can hear or read your personal messages.

The feature is rolling out in stages. It starts with a few languages, it is only on some devices for now, and it may not be available to you yet. The list of languages is limited at launch and grows as WhatsApp adds more.

sections.heading: How to turn it on and read a message
sections.body:
Transcripts are off until you turn them on.

1. Open WhatsApp and go to Settings.
2. Tap Chats.
3. Turn on Voice Message Transcripts.
4. Tap Choose language, then select the language most of the voice messages you receive are in.

To read a message, press and hold the voice message, then tap Transcribe.

sections.heading: Typing a reply by voice
sections.body:
WhatsApp's transcript feature reads messages you receive. To type your own reply by talking, you use your phone's keyboard.

On iPhone, tap the Dictate key in the bottom-right corner of the keyboard. If you do not see it, turn on Enable Dictation under Settings, General, Keyboard. On Android with Gboard, tap the microphone at the top of the keyboard. Talk-to-text does not work with every language, so check your keyboard language if it does not start.

sections.heading: When WhatsApp cannot transcribe a message
sections.body:
Some voice messages will not transcribe, for example when the language is not supported yet. For those, save the voice note as a file and open [Voice Note to Text](https://voice-note-to-text.lazur.app/).

Choose the file. The tool takes audio up to 15 MB, including .opus, .ogg and .m4a. The text comes back in about 1 to 3 seconds, and you can copy it with one click.

sections.heading: Check the text before you send it
sections.body:
A transcript is a fast draft, not a recording you can trust word for word. Play the voice message once while you read the text. Fix any name, number or place that looks wrong before you reply or pass the message on.

If a voice message is long, read it in two or three parts while you play it. You will catch mistakes sooner, and you can stop the playback at any point to check a word.

The free tool sends your file to Lazur's servers, where Google Gemini transcribes it. WhatsApp's transcripts run on your device, according to WhatsApp, so choose the route that fits the message.

If you write replies by voice all day, Lazur is a Mac app for it. Hold two keys and talk, and it types into whatever app you are in.

faq.q: Does WhatsApp have voice to text?
faq.a: Yes, on some devices and in some languages. WhatsApp can turn a received voice message into text when Voice Message Transcripts is on, under Settings, then Chats. If the feature is not available to you yet, save the voice note and transcribe it with the free tool.

faq.q: Can I turn a WhatsApp voice note into text?
faq.a: Yes, in two ways. If transcripts are on and support the language, press and hold the voice message and tap Transcribe. Otherwise, save the voice note as a file and upload it to Voice Note to Text, which returns the words in about 1 to 3 seconds.

faq.q: How do I use voice to text on WhatsApp?
faq.a: To read voice messages, turn on Voice Message Transcripts under Settings, then Chats, and press and hold a message to tap Transcribe. To type a reply by talking, use your phone keyboard's dictation key, because voice typing in WhatsApp runs through the keyboard.

faq.q: Is the Lazur voice note tool free?
faq.a: Yes, with limits. You get 3 free runs a day, and leaving an email gives you 3 more. No account is needed, and files can be up to 15 MB.

pages.h1: WhatsApp voice to text not working on iPhone

sections.heading: Check the WhatsApp transcript setting
sections.body:
Transcripts are off by default, and the setting lives inside WhatsApp, not in the iPhone Settings app.

1. Open WhatsApp and go to Settings.
2. Tap Chats.
3. Turn on Voice Message Transcripts.
4. Tap Choose language, then select the language most of your voice messages are in.

If you change the language later, change it here. Turning transcripts off resets the language, so set it again when you turn them back on.

sections.heading: Match the language
sections.body:
A transcript fails when it does not match the language of the voice message. WhatsApp's help page also lists background noise and unsupported languages as causes.

If one voice note fails and others work, the language of that note is the likely cause. Save that note and use the free tool below, which reads the language it hears.

If the other person sends voice messages in a language you do not usually set, that is a good reason to change the language in WhatsApp's Chats settings. Set it to the language most of their notes use, then test again with a new message from them.

sections.heading: Turn on Dictation for typing
sections.body:
If the trouble is the microphone you tap to type a reply, that is the keyboard's Dictation feature. Open Settings, tap General, tap Keyboard, and turn on Enable Dictation.

Then open WhatsApp, tap a text field, and tap the Dictate key in the bottom-right corner of the keyboard. Apple's steps are on [Dictate text on iPhone](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/dictate-text-iph2c0651d2/ios).

sections.heading: Transcribe the note here
sections.body:
When WhatsApp cannot read a voice message, save it as a file and upload it. The save option is in the share menu for the message, and the exact menu differs by WhatsApp version.

1. Save the voice note as an audio file.
2. Open [Voice Note to Text](https://voice-note-to-text.lazur.app/).
3. Choose the file. The tool takes audio up to 15 MB, including .opus, .ogg and .m4a.
4. Read the text and copy it with one click.

You get 3 free runs a day, and 3 more if you leave an email. No account is needed.

The result is a plain text version of what was said, with punctuation added. It is a good starting point for a reply, but read it once against the audio before you rely on it for anything important.

sections.heading: What happens to the file
sections.body:
The tool sends the file to Lazur's servers, where Google Gemini transcribes it. WhatsApp's transcripts are generated on your device, according to WhatsApp. Choose the route that suits a private message before you upload it.

If you do not want a voice note sent anywhere, use WhatsApp's own transcript on your iPhone once it is available to you, and leave the free tool for files you are happy to upload.

faq.q: Why is my voice to text not working on WhatsApp on iPhone?
faq.a: Check two things. First, WhatsApp's transcripts need Voice Message Transcripts turned on under Chats, with the right language. Second, the keyboard's microphone needs Enable Dictation under Settings, General, Keyboard. Then tap the Dictate key in the bottom-right corner of the keyboard.

faq.q: How do I enable speech to text in WhatsApp on iPhone?
faq.a: WhatsApp's own transcripts are in WhatsApp Settings under Chats, where you turn on Voice Message Transcripts and choose a language. For typing by talking, turn on Dictation under Settings, General, Keyboard, then tap the Dictate key on the keyboard.

faq.q: Can WhatsApp convert a voice message to text on iPhone?
faq.a: Yes, on some devices and in some languages. Turn on Voice Message Transcripts under Chats in WhatsApp Settings, then press and hold a voice message and tap Transcribe. If the message will not transcribe, save it and use the free tool.
